0|b2032fd567326ad0b2d443bb6d96d2580ec670a5|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"qla2xxx: kill sessions/log out initiator on RSCN and port down events
To fix some issues talking to ESX
column2: this patch modifies the qla2xxx driver

column1: so that it never logs into remote ports.  This has the side effect of
getting rid of the ""rports"" entirely
column2: which means we never log out of

column1: initiators and never tear down sessions when an initiator goes away.
This is mostly OK
column2: except that we can run into trouble if we have

column1: initiator A assigned FC address X:Y:Z by the fabric talking to us
then initiator A goes away.  Some time (could be a long time) later
initiator B comes along and also gets FC address X:Y:Z (which is
available again
column2: because initiator A is gone).  If initiator B starts

column1: talking to us
column2: then we'll still have the session for initiator A

column1: since we look up incoming IO based on the FC address X:Y:Z
will end up using ACLs for initiator A.
Fix this by:
1. Handling RSCN events somewhat differently; instead of completely
skipping the processing of fcports
an fcport disappears
column2: we tell the target code the tear down the

column1: session and tell the HBA FW to release the N_Port handle.
2. Handling ""port down"" events by flushing all of our sessions.  The
firmware was already releasing the N_Port handle but we want the
target code to drop all the sessions too.
